# Getting started

TxSuite is T5Suite, T7Suite and T8Suite in one program.
The three suites were rebuilt on .NET 10 and Avalonia, without the commercial components the old suites needed, so TxSuite runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.
Open a T5, T7 or T8 binary and TxSuite works on it the way that ECU's suite did: the same files read, edited and written, the same maps, tools and realtime panel.
It talks to the ECU through TrionicCANLib, the library of the Trionic CAN Flasher.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t5-manual"}
This manual covers TxSuite with a Trionic 5 binary.
Trionic 7 and Trionic 8 have a manual of their own, Help → T7 → User manual and Help → T8 → User manual.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t7-manual"}
This manual covers TxSuite with a Trionic 7 binary.
Trionic 5 and Trionic 8 have a manual of their own, Help → T5 → User manual and Help → T8 → User manual.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t8-manual"}
This manual covers TxSuite with a Trionic 8 binary.
Trionic 5 and Trionic 7 have a manual of their own, Help → T5 → User manual and Help → T7 → User manual.
:::

What all three ECU's have in common is written the same way in all three manuals.
The parts only your ECU has are in chapters of their own, right after the chapter they belong to.

## Installation

The newest TxSuite and TxExtras are on one page, <https://github.com/roffe/TuningSuites/releases/latest>.
All downloads are on the releases page: the `Txsuite_v…` releases, and `Txsuite_nightly` with the latest build.

The stock binaries of all three ECU's are a separate download, TxExtras.
TxSuite uses them wherever it needs the original file of a partnumber, Lookup partnumber for example.
They go into `Binaries\T5`, `Binaries\T7` and `Binaries\T8` in TxSuite's folder.

### Windows

Run TxSuiteSetup.exe.
It installs to `Program Files (x86)\MattiasC\TxSuite`, next to any old T5Suite, T7Suite or T8Suite (it replaces none of them), and asks whether `.bin` files should open in TxSuite.
Then TxExtrasSetup.exe puts the stock binaries into TxSuite's folder.
Running the setup of a newer build over an existing installation upgrades it.

Rather not install it?
TxSuite-win-x86.zip runs from wherever you unpack it, unpack TxExtras.zip into the `TxSuite` folder for the stock binaries.
It doesn't open `.bin` files by itself, and its update check opens the release page instead of downloading the setup.

### Linux

Download TxSuite-linux-x64.tar.gz (or -linux-arm64) and run it from where you extracted it.
Unpack TxExtras.zip into the `TxSuite` folder for the stock binaries.

```sh
tar xzf TxSuite-linux-x64.tar.gz
./TxSuite/TxSuite
```

`./TxSuite/install-desktop.sh` adds TxSuite to the application menu and to Open with for `.bin` files, for your user only.
Run it again after moving the folder.

The CombiAdapter needs libusb and the udev rule next to the program:

```sh
sudo cp TxSuite/70-txsuite.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger
```

There is also an AppImage, all of TxSuite in one file (TxSuite-linux-x64.AppImage, or -linux-arm64).
`chmod +x` it and start it.
It needs FUSE, which most desktops have; without it start it with `--appimage-extract-and-run`.
The stock binaries go next to the AppImage, unpack TxExtras.zip in its folder.
The udev rule isn't in the AppImage, take `70-txsuite.rules` from the tar.gz.

### macOS

Download TxSuite-osx-arm64.zip (Apple silicon) or -osx-x64 (Intel).
The build is not signed, so clear the quarantine flag after extracting it, then start it from Terminal or by double-clicking TxSuite in Finder:

```sh
unzip TxSuite-osx-arm64.zip
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine TxSuite
./TxSuite/TxSuite
```

## Supported interfaces

TxSuite supports the same interfaces as the Trionic CAN Flasher.
On a T5 it talks to the ECU's P-bus.

| Interface | Windows | Linux | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lawicel CANUSB | Lawicel CANUSB DLL driver | FTDI serial port | FTDI serial port |
| CombiAdapter | libusb (WinUSB driver) | libusb + udev rule | libusb |
| OBDLink SX / EX, ELM327 | serial port | serial port | serial port |
| Just4Trionic | serial port | serial port | serial port |
| SLCAN | serial port | serial port | serial port |
| Kvaser HS | Kvaser CANlib driver | Kvaser linuxcan | not supported |
| J2534 (Beta) | vendor DLL (32-bit) | vendor `.so` | not supported |
| Wideband lambda (realtime) | serial port | serial port | serial port |

The adapters still need their own drivers, see Adapter setup in the flasher's README, <https://github.com/roffe/Trionic#adapter-setup>.
Which adapter TxSuite uses is set in File → Settings → Common.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t5-manual"}
The P&E micro and USB BDM programmers of T5Suite are gone, there is no driver for them on .NET 10.
Reading and flashing goes over CAN, see the ECU menu.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="t7-manual"}
The P&E micro programmer of T7Suite is gone, there is no driver for it on .NET 10.
Reading and flashing goes over CAN, see the ECU menu.
:::

## Settings and log files

Settings and log files are in `%APPDATA%\MattiasC\TxSuite` on Windows and `~/.config/MattiasC/TxSuite` on Linux and macOS.
File → Settings → Logging decides which log files get written, at what level and for how long, and its Open button shows the folder on any system.

The first start takes over the settings of T5Suite, T7Suite and T8Suite once, with their Recent lists merged into one.
After that TxSuite keeps its own settings and the old suites are left alone.

## Coming from the old suites

TxSuite looks and works like the old suites, with some differences:

- One window for all three ECU's. The file you open decides the ECU.
- One menu bar instead of the ribbon. Want the ribbon back? File → Settings → Common → Show ribbon bar instead of menus.
- One settings dialog with a tab per ECU.
- Excel export and import are CSV now, and the map tables copy as text that pastes into Excel.
- Autologging, sound notifications, full screen and the panel snapshot (F9) are gone.
- New are the symbol and command palettes, colour blind modes, a dark skin, dropping files on the window and multi-step undo in the map viewer.

## Updates

TxSuite looks for a newer release when it starts and from Help → Check for updates, and shows the result in the status bar.
When there is one it asks.
OK downloads the setup on Windows and opens the release page elsewhere (and for the Windows zip).
